receipts.subject: docs/visual_quality/vq2/vq2_a2_r2_final_gate_a_r1.ai
receipts.observed: body, collar and closure rendered in their approved colours; logo, registered symbol, divider, Rose, Damascena and NIGHT REPAIR OIL all absent from the visible result
receipts.finding: The R1 colour repair worked - the three visible objects carry their approved colours, which R0 did not. A different defect remains: 37 of 40 objects do not reach the visible result. Measured in the repo, all 37 missing objects lie fully inside the body's bounding box and the 3 survivors are exactly those the body does not cover. That fits two explanations equally well - the body stacking above the artwork, or Illustrator discarding content after the third layer block - and this environment cannot separate them, so neither is recorded as the cause. R2 removes layer blocks and inherited state entirely, so it does not depend on which is true.

receipts.subject: docs/visual_quality/vq2/vq2_a2_r2_final_gate_a_r2.ai
receipts.observed: body, collar, closure, BBROSE logo, medallion and registered symbol, divider, Rose, Damascena and NIGHT REPAIR OIL all visible in approved colours, as separate Path and Compound Path objects
receipts.finding: This is the first Illustrator run of this artwork that lost nothing, and it closes the second defect: R1 rendered 3 of 40 objects, R2 renders all of them. Illustrator also built real vector objects rather than embedding the EPS - the owner reports separate Path and Compound Path items, so the compound paths carrying the counters and the medallion survived as objects. What it does NOT establish is Gate A. The returned .ai hashes exactly to the R2 source, so it is the original re-uploaded and nothing was saved, closed or reopened; a verification copy necessarily differs from the file it was saved from. Any uploaded PDF/PNG that matches this repository's own R2 proofs is likewise a re-upload and carries no Illustrator provenance. Neither upload reached this environment, so neither was hashed here.
receipts.does_not_isolate_r1_mechanism: R2 changed several things at once, so this does not say whether R1 lost its artwork to stacking or to a dropped layer boundary. Fixture A would still separate them; that is now forensic, not blocking.

receipts.subject: vq2_a2_r2_final_illustrator_verified.ai (as submitted)
receipts.finding: The first genuinely different file to come back, and a native Illustrator document rather than our EPS - a save really happened. Measured here from the file itself: 40 vector objects, 39 filled plus the divider stroke, all four approved colours and nothing else, zero rasters, zero live text. The artwork passed. The page did not: 763.654 x 983.225 pt against the accepted 207.1627 x 493.2283. The ink measures the same physical height as the source, so the artwork was translated, never resized. This is a defect in the automation script, not in the artwork.
receipts.second_finding: The result JSON on disk came from a DIFFERENT, aborted run in which the .jsx was selected instead of the .ai; it records FAIL with save, reopen and both exports false, and it overwrote the record belonging to the run that produced this copy. The copy is still genuine, but its script-written provenance was destroyed. Both script defects are now fixed.

Only a human performing the checks in Illustrator can establish that.
